Group Policy is an incredibly powerful tool to have at your disposal when working within a domain
environment. Many pre-built configurations and settings exist, and as you have seen, some are being
used whether you realize it or not, due to them being configured inside the Default Domain Policy.
Because Group Policy even has the power to manipulate the registry on client machines, the sky is
pretty much the limit on what you can manage on your client computers via GPOs.
Some of the most common ways I see Group Policy utilized are automatic drive mappings, printer
installations, desktop personalizations, centralized security standards, and password management.
Additionally, it can be used to push out RDS security policies, to lock down kiosk stations, to automati -
cally install applications, and so much more. Group Policy is even commonly used to assist companies
who are on cloud migration paths, through things such as centralized OneDrive administration.

A dominant eigenvalue has strictly greater absolute value than every other eigenvalue of a matrix. Repeated multiplication then makes its eigenvector component dominate a generic starting vector.

This behavior supports the [[Power Method]]. If the largest magnitudes are tied or the starting vector has no component in the dominant eigendirection, the expected convergence may fail.

A dominant strategy is so effective that a player has no meaningful reason to use an alternative. Its existence narrows the decision space and makes other mechanics strategically irrelevant.

Balance work should change costs, risks, counters, circumstances, or rewards so several strategies remain situationally useful. A strategy available to only one side can also make an asymmetric game unfair.

A Doppler satellite position fix compares the known transmitted frequency with the frequency received as a satellite approaches and recedes. If the satellite orbit is known, the shape and inflection of the frequency-shift curve constrain the receiver's location. Transit used this method for ships and submarines, but a useful fix required observing a pass and was difficult for fast-moving aircraft. GPS instead uses code travel time for rapid range measurements while still using Doppler-sensitive tracking for velocity and carrier acquisition.

A double Koszul complex combines exterior powers and symmetric powers with two compatible Koszul-style differentials. One direction uses the original sequence, while the other uses formal variables.

Taking cycles, boundaries, or homology along one direction produces [[Approximation Complex]]es. The construction relates relations among ideal generators to symmetric and Rees algebras.

A double quantization artifact is the periodic over- and under-population of transform-coefficient values produced by rounding at one step size and then at another. Some values from the first quantizer map disproportionately into the bins of the second, leaving a comb-like statistical pattern.

The pattern is evidence of two incompatible JPEG quantization histories and can sometimes be localized to edited regions. Its visibility depends on coefficient frequency, image content, alignment, and the relationship between the two tables.

A dramatic action is a player action that changes the direction of the plot and therefore the story events the player can experience later. It is more specific than an action that merely overcomes a gameplay challenge.

The game must communicate the action's consequences well enough for agency to be meaningful. A choice that changes only hidden data or reconverges immediately without perceptible effect may feel dramatic in code but not in experience.

A drawable game object exposes a draw operation used during the output phase of the [[Game Loop]]. It contributes visible representation without implying that the object must also change its state every frame.

Keeping drawing separate from [[Updateable Game Object]] behavior lets the world maintain distinct lists and supports objects that are only simulated, only rendered, or both.

A duplicated, darkened extraction of a performer can provide a shadow tied to the performer's own movement. In the book's crowd example, the lower part of that dark copy is blurred and directionally spread to make a moving core contact shadow, while a feathered dark shape supplies wider falloff. Stacking these contributions makes feet meet the floor without keyframing each footfall. Additional gradients can darken subjects behind nearer copies, suggesting mutual occlusion. The technique is especially useful for [[Crowd Replication with Animated Cards]].

A dynamic collision sweep accounts for object motion across a time interval by testing a shape along its displacement rather than only at its starting and ending positions. It reduces tunneling when fast objects cross thin obstacles between frames.

Relative motion can turn a moving-versus-moving query into one shape swept against another. The earliest valid time of impact identifies where response should begin before the remaining motion is considered.

A faceted plot repeats the same graphic for subsets of data in aligned panels. Shared scales and encodings make group-specific patterns easier to compare without combining every observation in one crowded display.

Free scales may reveal local variation but weaken direct comparison, so their use should be explicit.

A factor for one direction of a compatible conversion can be inverted for the reverse direction. Pryor's fuel-efficiency example uses a kilometers-per-mile ratio in the numerator but the reciprocal of liters-per-gallon in the denominator, so gallons cancel and liters remain below kilometers. Bidirectional conversion still requires choosing the correct orientation for each unit appearing in a compound expression. A reciprocal does not by itself handle scales with an offset, such as absolute Fahrenheit and Celsius readings. See [[Temperature Readings versus Intervals]].

A factor is a number or expression multiplied with another to produce a product. In

$$12x^2=3x\cdot4x,$$

(3x) and (4x) are factors of (12x^2). A factor must divide the product exactly within the number or expression system being used.

Recognizing factors permits cancellation in fractions and supports [[Polynomial Factorization]]. A common factor divides every term of a sum and can be taken outside parentheses through the [[Distributive Property]]. Terms joined by addition are not themselves cancellable factors until the expression is factored.

A factor loading is a coefficient connecting a latent factor to an observed variable or unit in a [[Factor Analysis]] model. Its magnitude and sign describe how strongly that factor contributes to the corresponding measurement pattern.

Loadings make a hidden direction interpretable by showing which variables move together with it. Their sign and scale can change with an equivalent rotation or factor convention, so interpretation focuses on relative patterns rather than an arbitrary orientation.

A factorable quadratic is a quadratic polynomial that can be expressed as a product of lower-degree factors over the number system being used. For example,

$$x^2+5x+6=(x+2)(x+3)$$

over the integers.

Factorability depends on the allowed coefficients. The polynomial (x^2-2) has no factorization into integer-coefficient linear factors, although it factors using irrational coefficients. When convenient factors are unavailable, a quadratic equation can still be solved through [[Completing the Square]] or the [[Quadratic Formula]].

A factory method centralizes the decision about which concrete implementation to create and returns it through a shared type. The inventory application's command factory maps textual input such as add, get, update, or quit to a corresponding command object, so the command loop need not contain each constructor and its dependencies. A new command changes the creation boundary rather than every caller that executes commands.

A failed prototype is productive when it reveals that an assumption about action, comprehension, technology, or experience was wrong. Discovering that mismatch early gives the team information while the design is still cheap to change.

The useful response is neither to hide the failure nor to treat it as proof that the entire idea is worthless. The team identifies what the result teaches, revises the question, and runs another cycle.

A faithful module is a module whose [[Module Annihilator]] is zero. No nonzero scalar acts as zero on every module element.

Any module M becomes faithful when regarded over the quotient R/Ann(M). Faithfulness therefore separates properties of the module action from ring elements that the action cannot detect.

A faithfully flat module is flat and also detects nonzero modules or failures of exactness after tensoring. Tensoring with it preserves and reflects the relevant algebraic information.

Faithful flatness lets properties such as regular sequences be checked after scalar extension. It is stronger than ordinary [[Flat Module|flatness]], which preserves exactness without necessarily detecting whether an object vanished.

A false alarm model represents the possibility that a sensor reports a detection even though the target or event is absent. A Boolean hidden variable can select between the ordinary sensor distribution and a false-alarm distribution.

Inference then considers both explanations instead of forcing every positive reading to be caused by the searched state. The prior probability and observation pattern determine how much support is assigned to the false-alarm branch.

A false negative occurs when a procedure fails to select a feature whose alternative hypothesis is true. It is a type II error and represents a missed signal rather than a spurious discovery.

Stricter thresholds can reduce [[False Positive|false positives]] while increasing false negatives. Useful high-throughput procedures therefore balance specificity against sensitivity instead of minimizing one error type without regard to the other.

A false positive occurs when a procedure declares a feature significant even though its null hypothesis is true. It is a type I error at the level of an individual decision.

When thousands of features are tested, several false positives can occur in one experiment. Multiple-testing procedures therefore summarize or control how these errors accumulate across the entire selected set.

A familiar unit name may refer to more than one defined scale, so a conversion table must preserve its qualifier. Pryor's alphabetical catalog distinguishes U.S. and Imperial gallons, U.S. dry and liquid quarts, ordinary and U.S. Survey feet, several British thermal unit definitions, computer and printer picas, and different kinds of year. Choosing a factor from the wrong variant changes the result without producing an obvious dimensional error: both ratios may still cancel correctly. The qualifier is therefore part of the unit, not optional decoration. See [[Unit Conversion Factor]] and [[Volume Unit Scaling]].

A fan-out-and-join computation distributes independent pieces of work to many workers or processors and later combines their results. Fan-out creates parallel activity; join waits for the required outputs and assembles them into the next stage.

The pattern can reduce elapsed time when work is sufficiently independent. Its benefits are limited by uneven task sizes, communication overhead, shared resources, and the need to validate results before joining them.

A Faraday [[Magnetohydrodynamic Generator]] extracts current across the duct in the direction perpendicular to both fluid flow and magnetic field. Electrodes on opposing walls collect the induced current as the conducting fluid crosses field lines. It differs from the Hall arrangement, which draws current along the flow direction. The electrode geometry is therefore part of how induced electrical power is collected.

A feasible solution satisfies every constraint and sign restriction of an optimization problem. The collection of all such points is the feasible region.

Feasibility is separate from quality: a feasible point need not be an [[Optimal Solution]]. If no point satisfies all constraints, the model is infeasible.

A feature area team coordinates several teams working within a broad area of the game. The grouping gives related work a coherent product goal and Product Ownership layer while preserving small delivery teams beneath it.

Feature areas should follow meaningful product boundaries and evolve as the game changes. Permanent silos can reproduce separate games inside one release.

A feature board visualizes the state of complete features across the disciplines working on them. Rows distinguish features that are active or waiting, columns show the kind of work underway, and priority remains visible as cards move toward done.

Unlike a task-centered board, it exposes whether code, art, animation, design, or testing is stalling playable value. It encourages swarming, limits parallel features, and creates time for integrated tuning before a Sprint ends.

A feature descriptor encodes the local image appearance around an interest point into a form that can be compared efficiently. A useful descriptor remains distinctive while tolerating expected changes in scale, rotation, illumination, or viewpoint.

Descriptors from the current camera image are searched against descriptors in a tracking model. A close descriptor match proposes a point correspondence, which geometry must then verify before it influences pose.

A feature is an attribute or variable used to describe an aspect of a data object. Useful features make objects distinguishable, support interpretable models, and provide the measurements on which classification, regression, clustering, retrieval, and other analytic tasks operate.

Feature meaning depends on the application. A color may be categorical, age numerical, and degree ordinal. The value of a feature is therefore inseparable from its domain, measurement scale, and the analytic question it is intended to answer.

A feature is relevant for unsupervised learning when it helps expose structure in the observations even though no class labels identify the desired groups. Relevance may mean preserving local neighborhoods, separating latent components, or supporting a compact and stable partition.

The difficulty is circular: clusters are used to judge features, while features determine the clusters that can be found. Practical methods therefore state an explicit structural criterion and compare candidate subsets or weights under that criterion.

A feature map records the output of one [[Convolutional Kernel]] at each location where the kernel is applied. It is a spatial account of how strongly the learned local detector responded across an image, not merely a single yes-or-no answer for the whole image.

A nonlinear [[Activation Function]] is commonly applied element by element to the map before a [[CNN Pooling Layer]] downsamples it. Maps from different kernels can also be combined and passed to a later convolutional layer. This lets the network build features from earlier detections while preserving spatial information until the architecture chooses to reduce it.

A feature team is a cross-discipline group able to deliver a player-facing feature across the components and crafts it requires. Its backlog and Sprint Goals are organized around integrated value instead of one technical layer.

Feature teams reduce handoffs and support [[Whole Game Focus]], but they require shared architecture, standards, and access to specialized knowledge to avoid duplicating or diverging foundational work.

A feature toggle separates deployment from exposure by allowing code already present in a live build to be enabled or disabled through configuration. Teams can integrate incomplete or experimental work without making it available to every player.

Toggles support staged testing and rapid rollback, but each one adds state and maintenance cost. Temporary toggles should be removed after their decision has been made.

A feature transformation function maps one or more existing variables to a derived variable. Unary functions operate on one input, binary functions combine two inputs, and compositions create deeper transformations.

The available functions form the grammar of automated feature construction. Type compatibility and semantic constraints prevent meaningless candidates, while composition depth controls expressiveness and search growth.

A feature transformation graph represents datasets as nodes and transformation operations as directed edges. A child node contains features produced from its parent, while combination nodes can unite features from several paths.

The graph records derivation history and exposes shared intermediate results. Because repeated composition creates a vast directed acyclic graph, exploration must prioritize promising nodes instead of materializing every possibility.

A feature vector is an ordered set of numerical measurements representing one observation. In speech recognition, it commonly summarizes the spectral properties of a short [[Speech Frame]].

A sequence of feature vectors is more compact and model-ready than the original waveform. The [[Acoustic Model]] uses the sequence to estimate which phonetic states most plausibly produced the signal.

More generally, a feature vector assigns one value to each feature selected for a data object. Using a fixed feature set places heterogeneous objects into a common coordinate representation, allowing learning algorithms to compare, partition, or predict them.

A feedback loop exists when changes produced by interacting parts return to influence the conditions that produced them. This circular causality turns a connected process into a [[Complex System]].

The two broad forms are the [[Reinforcing Loop]], which magnifies a direction of change, and the [[Balancing Loop]], which counteracts deviation. Complex behavior commonly arises from several such loops operating together at different levels and timescales.

A live product creates an operational loop when a team plans a change, develops and deploys it, measures player response, and uses that evidence to decide what follows. The value of speed lies in shortening the complete learning cycle rather than implementation alone.

A field automorphism is an isomorphism from a field to itself. Automorphisms fixing a base field leave each base element unchanged while possibly permuting algebraic roots.

Composition and inverse make the relevant automorphisms into a group.

A field is a nonzero [[Commutative Ring]] in which every nonzero element has a [[Multiplicative Inverse]]. Its only ideals are the zero ideal and the whole ring.

Every field is an [[Integral Domain]]. Conversely, a quotient by a [[Maximal Ideal]] is a field, so maximal ideals mark the places where a ring can be reduced to field-valued arithmetic.

The book moves from fields as special domains to fields as coefficient systems for polynomial division and as the base and extension objects of Galois theory. Finite domains and maximal-ideal quotients provide two important constructions of fields.

A field stores data inside a C# type or object. Instance fields belong to each object, while static fields belong to the type as a whole. A field can use any type, including arrays and collections.

Access modifiers control where a member is visible. Public exposes it broadly, private confines it to the declaring type, and protected or internal forms expose it to inheritance or an assembly boundary. Encapsulation chooses the narrowest visibility that still supports the intended collaboration.

A field-programmable gate array is a reconfigurable device whose logic, memory blocks, and communication paths can be arranged for a particular computation. It supports specialized pipelines and fine-grained parallelism without manufacturing a fixed custom chip.

Design effort and compilation time are higher than ordinary software, which motivates [[High-Level Synthesis]].

A figure caption communicates the figure's subject and interpretation, while a label enables stable cross-references. The pair makes a graphic part of the written argument rather than an unlabeled decoration.

A caption should identify encodings or conditions that are not obvious from the axes alone.

A filled bar chart scales every bar to the same total height and divides it into proportional segments. It emphasizes differences in composition across groups while intentionally discarding differences in group size.

Counts or sample sizes should accompany the plot when unequal totals affect interpretation.

A filler word is a spoken token or phrase that contributes little to the requested action, such as a hesitation or conversational preface. Natural speech contains these forms even when a formal command grammar does not expect them.

An NLU system can model or ignore fillers so they do not obscure the [[Intent]] and [[Entity|entities]]. Treating every word as equally semantic makes a voice interface unnecessarily brittle.

A filter bank divides the frequency spectrum of a speech frame into bands and measures the energy in each band. These measurements approximate the distribution of acoustic energy that distinguishes speech sounds.

The band energies form part of a [[Feature Vector]]. Applying the same bank across successive [[Speech Frame|frames]] produces a time-varying representation for an [[Acoustic Model]].

A filter feature selection model scores variables from general properties of the training data before a particular classifier is fitted. Common criteria measure correlation, information, dependency, consistency, or distance between classes.

Separating selection from classifier training makes filters comparatively efficient and reduces interaction between the selector's bias and the learner's bias. The tradeoff is that a high-scoring subset may not be optimal for the eventual classification algorithm.

Within a broader taxonomy, filters contrast with wrappers, hybrids, and embedded methods. Their model independence makes them reusable and scalable, although their scoring assumptions determine which dependencies they can recognize.

For high-dimensional Big Data, filters are attractive because they avoid fitting a classifier for every candidate subset. Distributed scoring can extend that advantage, although pairwise relevance and redundancy measures may still be expensive.

A filter method ranks or selects features before the final clustering algorithm is run. It uses properties of the data such as variance, redundancy, local geometry, or spectral consistency rather than feedback from a particular clusterer.

Filters are usually computationally efficient and reusable across algorithms. Their independence is also a limitation because a feature score can preserve generic structure without improving the specific grouping objective used downstream.

A filtered ring has a descending sequence R = R₀ ⊇ R₁ ⊇ R₂ ⊇ ··· such that RₘRₙ is contained in Rₘ₊ₙ. The index records increasing order or depth in the filtration.

Passing to successive quotients Rₙ/Rₙ₊₁ produces the [[Associated Graded Ring]]. Powers of an ideal give the important [[I-Adic Filtration]].

A fin central channel is a void created by subtracting an internal solid from the surrounding fin geometry. Its cross section and placement alter material volume, exposed surface, conduction paths, and the topology that must be meshed.

The subtracting object should be parameterized and aligned through explicit coordinates or a work plane. Measuring the completed channel and remaining tip features verifies that the Boolean difference produced the intended opening rather than an enclosed cavity or broken domain.

than other types such as spaghetti (the long stranded thin ones) [146]. The
author believes that this fast cooling must be due to the very good heat
dissipation properties, which can be explained by the rotini’s large surface
area. This hypothesis is investigated in this case study. A comparison is then
made with a straight slab to examine the effect of their shape difference.

A final regression model is the specification selected after candidate terms have been evaluated, discarded terms reconsidered, and relevant diagnostics reviewed. It is the adjusted model used to answer the prespecified hypothesis and support the main presentation table.

“Final” does not mean uniquely true. Another defensible selection path may produce a different specification, so the report should disclose the candidate set, selection process, reference groups, fit information, and sensitivity of the substantive conclusion.

A finite element node is a shared reference point at which unknown field values or degrees of freedom are defined. Adjacent elements meet at common nodes, allowing their local approximations to be connected.

Nodes carry different variables in different problems: displacement in structural analysis, temperature in thermal analysis, or potential in field problems. Shared nodal values enforce compatibility between neighboring elements during assembly.

A finite element temperature distribution is the interpolated thermal field obtained from solved nodal temperatures. Within a linear one-dimensional element, temperature varies linearly between its endpoint values.

The distribution reveals gradients that drive conductive heat flux. Comparing nodal results with analytical solutions provides a direct check on discretization, material assignment, and thermal boundary conditions.

A finite mixture model represents an observed distribution as a weighted combination of a fixed number of component distributions. The weights are positive and sum to one.

For clustering, each component is a group-specific data model. Fitting estimates its parameters and the latent memberships that best explain the observations.

A finite-state dialog manager represents an interaction as states connected by transitions. Each state defines expected input and assistant behavior, while recognized events determine the next state.

The model makes a narrow service flow predictable and testable. Its limitations appear when users change goals, provide information out of order, or require context not encoded in the state graph.

A finitely presented module P is projective if and only if P_p is projective over R_p for every prime ideal p; equivalently, it is enough to test every maximal ideal. Under the source's Noetherian finite-generation hypotheses, the localized modules are free.

The criterion makes projectivity a [[Local Property]]. Finite presentation ensures that maps and relations behave well enough under localization to recover the global splitting.

A firewall is a logical or physical boundary that allows or blocks network traffic according to defined rules. It can protect the edge of a cloud environment and separate internal security containers so only traffic appropriate to a service can cross.

Rules can restrict ports, protocols, sources, and destinations, while logs record rejected or accepted activity for monitoring. A firewall is one layer of defense and does not replace application authorization, endpoint protection, or secure data handling.

Within [[Defense in Depth]], a firewall regulates incoming and outgoing traffic at a network boundary according to a defined security policy. It can prevent an attack from moving freely between public and private networks, but it cannot repair a trusted user who executes a malicious payload.

A first-class function can be handled as a value: assigned to a variable, passed to another function, returned, or stored. C# delegates and lambdas give functions this role. A filter need not hard-code its comparison; the caller can pass a price or discount criterion, making the same traversal reusable for different selection rules.

A first-in, first-out backup rotation reuses or expires the oldest backup slot when a new one is created. A seven-day full-backup cycle, for example, replaces the first day's set on the eighth day and continues in order.

The same idea can alternate cloud providers rather than physical tapes. Under a differential scheme, one provider can hold a week's full baseline and differentials before the next week's sequence begins with another provider.

A first-person camera places the viewpoint at or near a character's eyes and derives its target from the viewing direction. Translation follows the character, while yaw and pitch control where the camera looks.

The design produces an immersive perspective but must manage rotation limits, input sensitivity, and field of view carefully. Visual geometry for the controlled body may require special treatment because it is unusually close to the camera.

A fission power plant uses reactor heat to raise steam, then passes that steam through a turbine-generator much like a [[Steam Power Plant]]. The source's comparison concerns the conversion arrangement: nuclear reaction replaces fuel combustion as the heat source, but thermal, mechanical, and electrical stages remain. This differs from the separate proposed [[Nuclear Fusion]] heat source discussed later in the book.

A fixed point of a function $g$ is a value $p$ satisfying $g(p)=p$. An equation $f(x)=0$ can often be rearranged into an equivalent fixed-point equation.

The rearrangement matters because different choices of $g$ can have different convergence behavior. [[Fixed-Point Iteration]] succeeds locally when the mapping contracts distances around the fixed point.

A fixed trained feedforward network applies the same layers and connections to each input, so its inference work does not grow with the particular input values. This predictable structure can support real-time deadlines once input size and architecture are fixed.

The claim concerns inference, not training or models with variable-length recurrence. Reliability still depends on whether new inputs resemble the conditions under which the network was evaluated.

A fixed-position box uses a containing block tied to the viewport in continuous media, so it remains in the same visible place while document content scrolls. Like [[CSS Absolute Positioning]], it is removed from normal flow.

In paged media, fixed content can be repeated in the same position on each page. Transformed ancestors and other context rules can alter which rectangle establishes the fixed containing block.

A fixed-price service model charges a stated amount for a defined period and scope. The price can combine a one-time setup amount with monthly, quarterly, or yearly recurring charges.

Fixing the price transfers some delivery, staffing, and quality risk to the provider through the [[Service Level Agreement]]. The consumer retains scope risk because it must decide whether the agreed service is sufficient for the work actually required.

A flat-plate collector admits sunlight through a transparent cover, absorbs it on a dark plate, and transfers heat through tubes to a working fluid. Insulation and casing reduce losses. It is commonly fixed and tilted toward the equator, can use both beam and diffuse radiation, and suits lower-temperature tasks such as water or space heating. Higher fluid temperature increases its heat loss.

A flat, nearly uniform sky may be improved by laying a new sky plate over it and masking that plate just above the horizon, rather than extracting every foreground boundary. Edge feather and reduced opacity let the two skies blend. A more complex sky or horizon demands roto, paint, or a procedural extraction to separate scene elements. In either case, the new sky's sun direction and atmospheric color must agree with the ground plate; the book flips a cloud plate when its light direction conflicts with shadows. See [[Feathering a Composite Edge]].

A flex formatting context arranges a container's direct children along a main axis and aligns them along a cross axis. It is primarily one-dimensional: a flex line distributes items in one direction even when wrapping creates several lines.

The axes follow [[CSS Flex Direction]] and the active writing mode rather than always meaning horizontal and vertical. Flexible sizing then distributes positive or negative free space among the items.

A flight briefing reviews the route, weather, NOTAMs, aerodrome conditions, aircraft state, planned exercises, takeoff and landing details, and relevant skills before departure. Longer flights may require preparation days in advance and information about fuel, fees, services, medical access, and alternates. The debrief afterward closes the learning and accountability loop.

A flight plan filed with a flight service organization or an itinerary left with a responsible person creates an external record of the intended route and arrival time. If the flight is not closed within the defined interval, that record supports search-and-rescue initiation. Opening, updating, and closing it are therefore operational safety actions rather than administrative paperwork alone.

A floated box is shifted to the left or right of its containing block until it reaches the container edge or another float. It is removed from ordinary block flow, while following inline content is shortened and wraps alongside it.

Floats affect one another and can move downward when insufficient horizontal space remains. Their behavior historically supported layouts as well as image-like text wrapping, although [[CSS Flexible Box Layout]] and [[CSS Grid Layout]] provide dedicated layout systems.

A floating table lets a typesetting system place the table near an appropriate location rather than exactly where its source appears. Captions and labels allow the prose to refer to it independently of placement.

Float behavior should be controlled carefully when order is essential to the argument.

A flowboard is a hybrid of a flowchart and storyboard used to document a game's structure. It shows gameplay modes, shell menus, and the conditions that move the player among them.

The diagram communicates experience flow more clearly than a list of screens. It also reveals unreachable modes, missing return paths, and transitions that ask the player to change controls or expectations without adequate explanation.

A fluid finite element represents pressure, velocity, temperature, potential, or related variables over a small flow-domain region. Two-dimensional elements may use three triangular nodes or four quadrilateral nodes.

Material properties, nodal coordinates, body loads, and surface conditions define the local equations. Assembled results can provide nodal pressures and velocities for steady or transient fluid systems.

A fly-by animation changes the viewer's virtual position and orientation around a static or changing three-dimensional scene. The source constructs a textured Earth and defines a sequence of geographic locations for the camera to visit. Unlike a [[Raster Map Animation]], the animated attribute may be the view itself rather than the data. Smooth paths, recognizable landmarks, and controlled speed preserve spatial orientation during the flight.

A foldback story is a branching interactive plot whose paths reconverge at planned inevitable events before branching again. It gives players local variation while limiting the combinatorial growth of wholly separate plot lines.

Reconvergence reduces production cost and preserves major dramatic beats. The branches still need distinct consequences or perspectives; otherwise the player learns that choices are cosmetic.

A follow camera maintains a chosen horizontal and vertical offset behind a moving target. The target's orientation determines the desired camera position and the direction in which the camera looks.

Directly snapping to the desired transform is simple but can transmit every abrupt target movement to the view. A [[Spring Follow Camera]] adds controlled lag and damping for smoother motion.
